sara_cs: FYI — ACME reported streaming cut out mid-payload on their Private deploy behind a corporate proxy. They see a partial SSE payload then connection closes, and on reconnect sometimes get a 401 for the stream resume token. Happened on multiple client versions. Trace: req=acme-req-7f3b

rahul_eng: ack — can you paste the raw client logs + one server trace? asking if this is auth TTL or proxy dropping idle window.

sara_cs: pasted logs from customer below. they say the stream sends ~2KB then a gap ~8-12s then close. token rotation is every 5m, token is valid. client log extract:
```
[2026-03-16T18:24:02Z] sse: got "data: {\"id\":1,\"chunk\":\"...\"}\n"
[2026-03-16T18:24:10Z] sse: no data for 11s, reconnecting
[2026-03-16T18:24:11Z] http: POST /v1/streams/resume 401
```

mike_sre: interesting — proxy could be doing TCP RST/idle timeout. What does `ssldump`/tcpdump show at the on-prem ingress? any FIN/RST from proxy? also curious if we're seeing HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE starvation if they tunnel via HTTP/2 proxy.

rahul_eng: another angle — we added a keepalive in our runtime that sends a zero-length event every 10s for corp-proxy churn. If the proxy normalizes to 15s idle timeout, gap shouldn't trigger. But if proxy rewrites SSE (some proxies buffer until CRLFCRLF) that could kill the stream. Can you ask them to run a curl test to compare?

sara_cs: asked them to run this curl against their ingress (they ran it at 18:30):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  https://private.acme.example/api/v1/stream?model=redwood-lite
```
They sent back tcpdump showing connection close with RST from proxy at 11s.

mike_sre: RST at 11s smells like a proxy keepalive mismatch. Also note the 401 on resume — could be our resume endpoint getting a new session id because the proxy rewrote or dropped cookies/headers on reconnect. Does the client retry with same auth header?

rahul_eng: if proxy strips or caches `Authorization` on reconnect (some proxies treat POSTs differently), the resume handshake could lose the header. We have a reproduce plan: (1) run an nginx sidecar configured to simulate corp proxy with idle_timeout 10s and header stripping, (2) reproduce SSE with token rotation and observe resume failures. I can spin a small repro on my laptop.

sara_cs: customer confirmed they use an older corporate edge appliance (vendor: GateProxy v2) that enforces HTTP/1.1 translation and has aggressive 'half-closed' timeouts. They also terminate TLS and then open new upstream TLS.

mike_sre: OK, that explains it. GateProxy's translation to HTTP/1.1 will break SSE semantics and likely buffer/flush behavior. Two failure modes here: (A) proxy RSTs after perceived idle leading to truncated payloads (partial output), (B) reconnect losing Authorization header -> 401 on resume which then leads to a full new session (billing/dup tokens).

rahul_eng: proposed mitigations for customer (short term):
- enable our streaming keepalive interval to 5s (forced) so proxy sees steady traffic
- change resume flow to accept a short-lived one-time resume token in query param (falls back to header) to handle proxies that strip headers on reconnect
- recommend GateProxy config: keepalive 30s and preserve Authorization header on upstream reconnects

sara_cs: customer asked for clear repro steps they can run. rahul, can you share the nginx sidecar config + exact curl repro?

rahul_eng: yep. quick nginx conf snippet I used (simulate header strip + 10s idle):
```
proxy_read_timeout 10s;
proxy_set_header Authorization ""; # simulate stripping
chunked_transfer_encoding off; # force buffering behavior
```
curl resume repro flow I used:
1) open stream: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://localhost:8443/stream`
2) wait 11s for proxy to RST -> observe partial chunk + connection close
3) attempt resume: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://localhost:8443/streams/resume -d '{"cursor":"..."}' -v` -> observe 401 when header stripped

mike_sre: to be safe, we'll also add transient logging on resume endpoint to emit `x-resume-source` (new header we add) and log when auth header missing so we can match customer traces without full payloads. I'll coordinate a small patch to runtime to accept resume token in query param for Private deployments behind corp proxies (opt-in flag).

sara_cs: customer appreciated reproducible plan. asked for ETA on short-term mitigations (keepalive tweak + resume-header-tolerant fallback).

rahul_eng: can do keepalive override ASAP (config flag) and the resume-query-param fallback in a small hotfix — estimate 3 business days for rollout to Private images. mike_sre, do you need an RFC?

mike_sre: log change + opt-in runtime flag is fine, no RFC needed. I'll schedule an ops window to push to their Private cluster once vetted.

sara_cs: perfect. I'll relay timeline and repro steps to ACME. Thanks team :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident 2026-03-16-ACME-STREAM created (priority: P2). Links: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-03-16-ACME-STREAM

rahul_eng: filing a small internal note in /eng-runtime about GateProxy translation patterns so others recognize this class of issue.

sara_cs: filing ticket with customer-facing summary and attaching the nginx repro excerpt and tcpdump. will update thread when ACME confirms keepalive test.
